items.title: Who should profit when AI comes to town?…
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: AI data centers are popping up across the US — and the people living next to them are increasingly upset.
Brian Janous, whose company finds land for some of the biggest data centers, hears those objections firsthand.
He proposes a solution that would change who benefits from the AI boom, putting a bigger share of the wealth directly into the hands of local communities.

items.title: The “godfather of AI” on the risks that …
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: Geoffrey Hinton helped create the neural networks behind today’s AI, won a Nobel Prize for it — and has spent the years since warning about where it’s headed.

In conversation with journalist Nicholas Thompson, Hinton shares the AI risks he’s worried about, sketches out a best-case future for the technology and explores whether or not chatbots have subjective experience.
Plus: hear his thoughts on the one rule we must give superintelligent AI.

items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: Why have we not yet found proof of alien life?
According to astrophysicist Avi Loeb, we simply haven't dedicated the proper resources.

Diving into unidentified phenomena such as the Oumuamua asteroid, he explores his scientific search for extraterrestrial technology, envisioning a future where a higher interstellar intelligence helps us improve life here on Earth.

items.title: What you hear when you stop talking | Jo…
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: Scientists have estimated how many colors we can see and how many scents we can smell … but director John Lloyd can’t find anyone who has counted how many sounds we can hear.
Drawing on a legendary career in radio, film and TV, he makes a funny case for paying closer attention to sound — and for listening more than you talk.
(Plus: find out why almost every frog noise you hear in movies sounds the same.) Hosted on Acast.
